title: Programmable skin: a cellular actuator you can address
question: Could you build skin that changes appearance on command, and what is the actual engineering object? A cephalopod chromatophore is a real actuator with a real datasheet - a pigment sac opened by radial muscle under direct motor-neuron control, expanding in about a tenth of a second - sitting on an optical stack that works by a different mechanism and runs a hundred times slower. This page lays out the routes into that system at eight scales, and is deliberately blunt about how few of them anyone can currently take.

scales.label: Molecular - pigment and protein
scales.blurb: Ommochrome synthesis and the reflectin proteins. This is where the only two demonstrated cephalopod genetic manipulations live, and both of them REMOVE pigment rather than control it.

scales.label: Organelle - the optical stack
scales.blurb: The Bragg reflector inside an iridophore and the pigment sacculus inside a chromatophore. The best-measured objects in the whole design space: layer counts, both refractive indices, both thicknesses and the tuning range are published numbers from LIVE cells.

scales.label: Cell - the chromatophore as an actuator
scales.blurb: A pigment sac opened by 15-25 radial muscle fibres under direct motor-neuron control. Our own mechanics model says the stroke is limited by the elastic sacculus, not by the muscle, which makes most muscle-side interventions useless.

scales.label: Circuit - how many independent channels
scales.blurb: Motor units, polyneuronal innervation and sub-chromatophore sectors. Measured in beautiful detail and manipulable almost not at all: every route here is a recording or a stimulation, not a construction.

scales.label: Development - laying out an addressable array
scales.blurb: A cuttlefish goes from a few thousand chromatophores to a few million while keeping the light:dark ratio constant and inserting new units far from old ones. The layout rule is measured; nothing has been intervened on.

scales.label: Genetic access - can you build anything at all
scales.blurb: The gate on the entire cephalopod half of this design space. Two knockouts exist. No transgene has been expressed in a cephalopod chromatophore.

scales.label: Vertebrate chromatophores - the tractable substrate
scales.blurb: Teleost and amphibian chromatophores move pigment on microtubules rather than by muscle: roughly an order of magnitude slower, and vastly more genetically tractable. A serious alternative substrate, not a footnote.

scales.label: Synthetic and non-living - the honest comparator
scales.blurb: What a funder will ask about. A 16x16 addressable colour-changing sheet was built in 2014 and switches in 1-2 s; commercial electrophoretic panels run at 300 ppi. Any biological route must beat these on some axis.

routes.title: Knock out tryptophan 2,3-dioxygenase to delete ommochrome pigment
routes.intervention: CRISPR-Cas9 ribonucleoprotein against tdo, injected into early Doryteuthis pealeii embryos.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Eyes and chromatophores lose their pigment: an unpigmented animal whose chromatophore organs are still present and still innervated, but have nothing to show. Knockout efficiency routinely above 90%.
routes.mechanism: TDO catalyses the first committed step of ommochrome synthesis from tryptophan; without it the pigment granules are never filled.
routes.reversibility: None. A germline or early-embryo edit is permanent.
routes.lethality_risk: Low for the edit itself in D. pealeii embryos; the species cannot currently be cultured through its life cycle, which is the real limit.
routes.difficulty: Demonstrated. This is the precedent the whole field rests on.

evidence.cite: Crawford K et al. 2020, Curr Biol 30:3484-3490.e4, 'Highly Efficient Knockout of a Squid Pigmentation Gene'

routes.title: Double knockout of tdo and ido to get a heritable albino line
routes.intervention: CRISPR-Cas9 against both tdo and ido in Euprymna berryi, bred to homozygosity over generations.
routes.predicted_phenotype: A true albino squid line that breeds true, used for two-photon calcium imaging of brain activity through the unpigmented tissue.
routes.mechanism: E. berryi carries an indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase that catalyses the same reaction as TDO, so single tdo knockouts stayed pigmented; removing both closes the pathway.
routes.lethality_risk: Low: the line is viable and fertile through multiple generations.
routes.difficulty: Demonstrated, and it took an unexpected second gene to work. The surprise is the lesson: cephalopod biochemistry is not annotated well enough to predict which single gene is sufficient.

evidence.cite: Ahuja N et al. 2023, Curr Biol 33:2774-2783.e5, 'Creation of an albino squid line by CRISPR-Cas9 and its application for in vivo functional imaging of neural activity'

routes.title: Time the CRISPR injection to set the degree of pigmentation
routes.intervention: Deliver the tdo ribonucleoprotein at chosen points in early development rather than at the earliest possible stage.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Graded pigmentation between wild type and unpigmented, set by how late the edit arrives relative to the lineage's divisions.
routes.mechanism: Later delivery leaves more already-committed cells unedited, so the mosaic fraction is a function of injection time.
routes.reversibility: None, but the SETTING is chosen before the animal exists.
routes.difficulty: Demonstrated. Worth flagging because it is the only analogue control knob anyone has over a cephalopod chromatophore property, and it is a one-shot developmental dial, not a runtime one.

evidence.cite: Crawford K et al. 2020, Curr Biol 30:3484-3490.e4, 'Highly Efficient Knockout of a Squid Pigmentation Gene'

routes.title: Engineer reflectin for a higher condensed-state refractive index
routes.intervention: Alter reflectin's conserved RLDQSY/RMDQSH-type motif composition to raise the refractive index of the condensed protein phase, then express it in iridophores or in a film.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Higher peak reflectance and a wider reachable gamut at the same layer count and the same tuning range.
routes.mechanism: Live-cell lamellae sit at n = 1.405 +/- 0.012 against an inter-lamellar space at 1.34, a contrast of only 1.048. Reflectance of a Bragg stack is set by that ratio raised to the power of twice the pair count.
routes.reversibility: n/a - a protein design change, not a runtime dial.
routes.lethality_risk: Unknown in vivo; reflectin assembly is tied to osmotic water expulsion, so a variant that condenses harder may not cycle.
routes.difficulty: High. No one has shown a designed reflectin variant with a raised condensed-phase index in a living cell.

evidence.cite: Ghoshal A et al. 2013, J R Soc Interface 10:20130386, 'Optical parameters of the tunable Bragg reflectors in squid'
Ghoshal A et al. 2014, J R Soc Interface 11:20140106, 'Experimental determination of refractive index of condensed reflectin in squid iridocytes'
Guan Z et al. 2017, Curr Biol 27:2833-2842.e6, 'Origin of the Reflectin Gene and Hierarchical Assembly of Its Protein'
Wolde-Michael E et al. 2021, Sci Rep 11:14580, 'Design and fabrication of recombinant reflectin-based multilayer reflectors: bio-design engineering and photoisomerism induced wavelength modulation'
evidence.note: recombinant reflectin multilayers, in a film, not a cell

routes.title: Change which ommochrome fills the sacculus
routes.intervention: Perturb the ommochrome branch downstream of TDO to shift the pigment a chromatophore makes between the yellow, red and brown species.
routes.predicted_phenotype: A chromatophore whose absorption edge moves, changing the hue it contributes at the same expansion state.
routes.mechanism: Squid chromatophores of different colours carry distinguishable metabolite fingerprints, and xanthommatin is localised to the light class in cuttlefish, so pigment identity and colour class covary.
routes.reversibility: Unknown; chromatophores darken irreversibly with age in the wild type.
routes.difficulty: High, and badly under-specified: no measured absorption spectrum for any cephalopod ommochrome was found, so the target hues cannot be stated.

evidence.cite: Bagwe K et al. 2026, Journal of proteome research , 'Metabolomic Profiling of Squid Chromatophores Reveals Differential Biochemical Fingerprints across Red, Yellow, and Brown Colors.'
Reiter S et al. 2018, Nature 562:361-366, 'Elucidating the control and development of skin patterning in cuttlefish'

routes.title: Change the number of lamella pairs in the iridophore Bragg stack
routes.intervention: Alter the number of reflectin-filled lamellae per stack from the eight or nine that contribute in live cells.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Peak reflectance rises steeply with pair count while the peak wavelength is unchanged. In our transfer-matrix model, going from eight to nine pairs - the whole range a live cell shows - raises the achievable gamut area by 15%, and peak reflectance at 550 nm climbs from 0.002 at one pair to 0.187 at ten.
routes.mechanism: A quarter-wave stack's admittance scales as (n_H/n_L) raised to twice the pair count, so at this very low index contrast more pairs is the cheapest way to brighten the reflector.
routes.difficulty: High: nobody has manipulated lamella number. The pair count is MEASURED (eight or nine live, six or seven after chemical fixation); only the intervention is hypothetical.

evidence.cite: Ghoshal A et al. 2013, J R Soc Interface 10:20130386, 'Optical parameters of the tunable Bragg reflectors in squid'

routes.editorial_note: Written, cut to meet a route-count range, then restored when that range turned out to be a floor. See NOTES.md for the reason it was nearly cut.

routes.title: Phosphorylate reflectin to condense it and switch the reflector on
routes.intervention: Drive the native acetylcholine-triggered phosphorylation cascade in iridophores, or phosphorylate recombinant reflectin in vitro.
routes.predicted_phenotype: The lamellae condense, expel water, thin, and the stack's refractive index contrast rises: reflectance appears and the peak moves to shorter wavelengths.
routes.mechanism: Phosphorylation neutralises reflectin's net charge, allowing hierarchical assembly and osmotic water expulsion from the lamellae.
routes.reversibility: Reversible in the animal; this is the native switching mechanism.
routes.difficulty: Demonstrated as a natural mechanism. Driving it ON COMMAND in a chosen cell is not demonstrated.

evidence.cite: Izumi M et al. 2010, J R Soc Interface 7:549-60, 'Changes in reflectin protein phosphorylation are associated with dynamic iridescence in squid'
DeMartini DG et al. 2015, J Biol Chem 290:15238-49, 'Structures, Organization, and Function of Reflectin Proteins in Dynamically Tunable Reflective Cells'
Wardill TJ et al. 2012, Proc Biol Sci 279:4243-52, 'Neural control of tuneable skin iridescence in squid'

routes.title: Stimulate skin nerves to tune iridophore colour and brightness
routes.intervention: Electrical stimulation of neurons in isolated Doryteuthis pealeii skin, with acetylcholine released within the iridophore layer.
routes.predicted_phenotype: The reflected peak shifts by more than 145 nm to shorter wavelengths and peak reflectance rises by more than 245%. Critically, the colour shift takes 17 s and the brightness change 32 s - two orders of magnitude slower than a chromatophore.
routes.mechanism: Two distinct mechanisms: reflectin condensation accounts for the reflectance change, while the faster colour shift is unexplained by it and the authors say so.
routes.difficulty: Demonstrated. The design consequence is severe and usually glossed over: the optical stack and the pigment actuator cannot be used together for a fast pattern, because one of them needs half a minute.

evidence.cite: Wardill TJ et al. 2012, Proc Biol Sci 279:4243-52, 'Neural control of tuneable skin iridescence in squid'

routes.title: Switch the leucophore backing under the stack
routes.intervention: Add, remove or tune the broadband-scattering leucophore layer beneath the iridophores.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Chromaticity is essentially unchanged - in our model the gamut area moves by 0% - while peak luminance falls by a factor of five when the backing is removed. It is a brightness layer, not a colour layer.
routes.mechanism: A diffuse white backing returns the light the partially-reflecting Bragg stack transmits, raising Y without changing the spectral shape much.
routes.difficulty: High as an intervention. Tunable leucophores are measured in female Doryteuthis opalescens, so the cell type is real and known to be dynamic.

evidence.cite: DeMartini DG et al. 2013, J Exp Biol 216:3733-41, 'Dynamic biophotonics: female squid exhibit sexually dimorphic tunable leucophores and iridocytes'
Ghoshal A et al. 2013, J R Soc Interface 10:20130386, 'Optical parameters of the tunable Bragg reflectors in squid'

routes.title: Soften the pigment sacculus so the same muscle opens it further
routes.intervention: Reduce the elastic sacculus's shear modulus - genetically, by altering its structural protein, or pharmacologically.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Not more stroke, and much slower return. In our sweep the steady-state ratio is already saturated at 2.56 at and below the fitted stiffness, so softening buys nothing there - but it costs retraction steeply: halving the fitted modulus raises the 90% retraction from 295 ms to 543 ms, and at a twentieth of it the organ does not return 90% of the way within six seconds. Stiffening trades the other way: at four times the fitted modulus retraction falls to 120 ms and the ratio collapses to 1.32.
routes.mechanism: Expansion is a balance between active radial-muscle force and the sacculus's elastic restoring force; retraction is driven by that same elasticity alone against the dermal drag, so stiffness sets return speed directly. Above the fitted value it also starts to cost stroke.
routes.difficulty: High. The sacculus shear modulus has never been measured in any paper we read; it is the one FITTED parameter in our mechanics model, so this route is a prediction about a quantity nobody has a number for.

evidence.cite: Hadjisolomou SP et al. 2021, Front Physiol 12:675252, 'Quantifying the Speed of Chromatophore Activity at the Single-Organ Level in Response to a Visual Startle Stimulus in Living, Intact Squid'
Cloney RA & Florey E 1968, Z Zellforsch Mikrosk Anat 89:250-80, 'Ultrastructure of cephalopod chromatophore organs'
evidence.note: the classic ultrastructure paper; cited from its PubMed record, not read

routes.title: Add radial muscle fibres to the chromatophore rosette
routes.intervention: Increase the number of radial muscle fibres per organ beyond the measured 15-25.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Almost nothing. In our model the expansion ratio rises from 1.62 at 8 fibres to its plateau well before the wild-type count, because the stroke is set by the sacculus's elasticity and not by available force. This is a NEGATIVE design result and the most useful thing our mechanics model says.
routes.mechanism: Across every sweep the organ is elastic-limited rather than stroke-limited at the baseline geometry, so extra parallel force actuators buy stroke only until the elastic load is overcome.
routes.difficulty: High, and our own model says not worth doing.

evidence.cite: Renard MDM et al. 2026, Elife 15, 'Disentangling cephalopod chromatophores motor units with computer vision'
Ukrow J et al. 2025, Elife 14, 'A computational pipeline to track chromatophores and analyze their dynamics'
evidence.note: 10-20 in the abstract; ~10-15 in the same paper's histology

evidence.cite: Suzuki M et al. 2011, PLoS One 6:e18244, 'Chromatophore activity during natural pattern expression by the squid Sepioteuthis lessoniana: contributions of miniature oscillation'

routes.title: Lengthen the radial fibres' reach to the dermal anchor
routes.intervention: Increase the anchor radius, so each fibre's contraction sweeps the sacculus rim further.
routes.predicted_phenotype: A larger stroke: in our sweep the area ratio rises monotonically with anchor radius, and the organ passes out of the stroke-limited regime.
routes.mechanism: A Hill-type fibre's absolute shortening is a fixed fraction of its length, so a longer fibre moves the rim further for the same strain.
routes.difficulty: High. The anchor radius is one of our ASSUMED parameters: the source describes 'an extremely elongated distal end' with no number.

evidence.cite: Senft SL et al. 2021, J Morphol 282:1245-1258, 'Networks of linked radial muscles could influence dynamic skin patterning of squid chromatophores'

routes.title: Expand a chromatophore on command with glutamate
routes.intervention: Local application of L-glutamate to skin, or agonists at the AMPA/kainate and NMDA-like receptors of the chromatophore neuromuscular junction.
routes.predicted_phenotype: The chromatophore expands, and its transmission spectrum shifts towards lighter colours as the granule layer thins.
routes.mechanism: Motor neurons make excitatory glutamatergic synapses onto the radial muscles; nitric oxide mediates part of the glutamate-dependent pathway in Sepia.
routes.lethality_risk: n/a in an isolated preparation; systemic glutamate agonists in a live animal are a different question and we did not find one addressed.
routes.difficulty: Demonstrated. It is a bath, not an address: it drives every chromatophore it reaches, so it is a chemistry control and not a spatial one.

evidence.cite: Reiter S et al. 2018, Nature 562:361-366, 'Elucidating the control and development of skin patterning in cuttlefish'

Lima PA et al. 2003, Eur J Neurosci 17:507-16, 'AMPA/kainate and NMDA-like glutamate receptors at the chromatophore neuromuscular junction of the squid: role in synaptic transmission and skin patterning'
Mattiello T et al. 2010, J Biol Chem 285:24154-63, 'Nitric oxide mediates the glutamate-dependent pathway for neurotransmission in Sepia officinalis chromatophore organs'

routes.title: Use the myogenic rhythm and its serotonergic brake as a second channel
routes.intervention: Apply serotonin, or block it, in skin showing spontaneous myogenic chromatophore activity.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Spontaneous chromatophore oscillation is suppressed or released, independently of the motor-neuron drive.
routes.mechanism: Squid chromatophore networks show myogenic activity under serotonergic inhibition - a slow modulatory channel layered on top of the fast glutamatergic one.
routes.difficulty: Demonstrated in preparation. Interesting for a designer because it is a SECOND, chemically distinct control channel over the same actuator.

evidence.cite: Rosen HE & Gilly WF 2017, J Exp Biol 220:4669-4680, 'Myogenic activity and serotonergic inhibition in the chromatophore network of the squid Dosidicus gigas (family Ommastrephidae) and Doryteuthis opalescens (family Loliginidae)'
Suzuki M et al. 2011, PLoS One 6:e18244, 'Chromatophore activity during natural pattern expression by the squid Sepioteuthis lessoniana: contributions of miniature oscillation'
evidence.note: miniature oscillations contributing to natural pattern expression

routes.title: Cut or add the muscle-to-muscle links between neighbouring chromatophores
routes.intervention: Sever, or engineer, the direct radial-muscle contacts between adjacent chromatophore organs.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Changed spatial correlation between neighbouring units at unchanged neural drive: a mechanically blurrier or sharper skin.
routes.mechanism: Radial muscles of neighbouring chromatophores make direct contacts, so the array has mechanical coupling the wiring diagram does not show.
routes.difficulty: High. The anatomy is described; the functional consequence is the authors' own suggestion ('could influence') and has not been tested.

evidence.cite: Senft SL et al. 2021, J Morphol 282:1245-1258, 'Networks of linked radial muscles could influence dynamic skin patterning of squid chromatophores'

routes.editorial_note: Written, cut to meet a route-count range, then restored when that range turned out to be a floor. See NOTES.md for the reason it was nearly cut.

routes.title: Measure how many independent channels drive ONE chromatophore
routes.intervention: Divide each chromatophore into 36 polar slices, track slice areas at 20 fps, and separate the sources by PCA followed by ICA.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Each chromatophore is driven by 3.715 +/- 1.211 independent sources (1829 cells, sedated), each innervating a contiguous petal-shaped domain of 3 to 16 of the 36 slices. Sedation does not change it (3.683 +/- 1.224 unsedated, p = 0.83).
routes.mechanism: Polyneuronal innervation with non-overlapping angular territories, so a single chromatophore is roughly four independent actuators and not one.
routes.lethality_risk: Animals were head-fixed, sedated or not; this is terminal or near-terminal work.
routes.difficulty: Demonstrated. This is the single most important number in the design space for anyone building an addressable skin: the pixel is not the cell.

evidence.cite: Renard MDM et al. 2026, Elife 15, 'Disentangling cephalopod chromatophores motor units with computer vision'

routes.title: Fire one motor neuron and watch its field expand
routes.intervention: Intracellular stimulation of a single chromatophore-lobe motor neuron with simultaneous high-speed video of the skin.
routes.predicted_phenotype: About five nearby chromatophores each expand partially and directionally, in petals pointing at a common virtual centre - not whole cells switching on. Some units instead expand isotropically, and the authors report that too.
routes.mechanism: One motor neuron's terminals reach contiguous angular sectors of several adjacent chromatophores, forming a 'virtual chromatophore'.
routes.difficulty: Demonstrated, and technically hard.

evidence.cite: Renard MDM et al. 2026, Elife 15, 'Disentangling cephalopod chromatophores motor units with computer vision'

routes.title: Map motor units by minimal stimulation of distal nerve branchlets
routes.intervention: Threshold electrical stimulation of nerve branchlets in freshly dissected dorsal mantle skin, scoring which chromatophores expand.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Small monochromatic units of 2-10 chromatophores, usually clustered, with a median radius of 2.5 chromatophores or 247 um. Light units are harder to stimulate in isolation than dark ones, suggesting smaller axons.
routes.mechanism: Each motor neuron innervates a small, colour-pure, spatially clustered set.
routes.difficulty: Demonstrated.

evidence.cite: Reiter S et al. 2018, Nature 562:361-366, 'Elucidating the control and development of skin patterning in cuttlefish'

routes.title: Microstimulate the optic lobe to call up body-pattern components
routes.intervention: Focal electrical stimulation at sites across the squid optic lobe.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Discrete, repeatable body-pattern components appear, organised mosaically rather than somatotopically across the lobe.
routes.mechanism: The optic lobe holds a mosaic map of pattern components, not of skin position, so the addressing above the motoneurons is by PATTERN, not by place.
routes.difficulty: Demonstrated. For a designer, this says the natural control hierarchy compresses the skin into a pattern vocabulary - which is also what the 9-dimensional transition manifold below says.

evidence.cite: Liu TH & Chiao CC 2017, J Neurosci 37:768-780, 'Mosaic Organization of Body Pattern Control in the Optic Lobe of Squids'

routes.title: Exploit the low dimensionality of real pattern transitions
routes.intervention: Track 17,305 chromatophores at 60 frames per second through repeated dark-to-light startle transitions and project into principal components.
routes.predicted_phenotype: The animal moves through very similar intermediate states every time, with 85% of the variance in 9 dimensions - from a 17,305-dimensional actuator array.
routes.mechanism: Neural constraints, not mechanical ones, restrict the paths pattern transitions can take; nothing physical forbids a direct route.
routes.difficulty: Demonstrated. This is the strongest empirical argument that a programmable skin needs far fewer channels than it has actuators, and it is a measured number rather than our model's.

evidence.cite: Reiter S et al. 2018, Nature 562:361-366, 'Elucidating the control and development of skin patterning in cuttlefish'

routes.title: Size the controller: how many channels, at what motor-unit size
routes.intervention: Sweep the number of independent control channels and the motor-unit size against pre-declared target patterns in a model array at the measured chromatophore density, and find the knee.
routes.predicted_phenotype: See the control-channels study for the measured knee and its spread across seeds. The headline is a channel count per unit skin area, which is the spec sheet anyone building this needs.
routes.mechanism: Below the knee the skin cannot cover the target; above it, extra channels address actuators that are already driven by a neighbour.
routes.difficulty: Our own study. Every structural input is measured (array density, motor-unit sizes, expansion ratio); the observer's acuity is assumed.

evidence.cite: Reiter S et al. 2018, Nature 562:361-366, 'Elucidating the control and development of skin patterning in cuttlefish'
Renard MDM et al. 2026, Elife 15, 'Disentangling cephalopod chromatophores motor units with computer vision'
Hadjisolomou SP et al. 2021, Front Physiol 12:675252, 'Quantifying the Speed of Chromatophore Activity at the Single-Organ Level in Response to a Visual Startle Stimulus in Living, Intact Squid'

species_of_evidence: model; anchored in Sepia officinalis, Euprymna berryi and Doryteuthis pealeii, which is three animals

routes.title: Close the loop in the skin itself with dermal photoreception
routes.intervention: Use the opsin and phototransduction machinery already present in chromatophores to make the skin respond to local light without the brain.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Local, brain-independent modulation of chromatophore state by the light falling on that patch of skin.
routes.mechanism: Rhodopsin, retinochrome and the phototransduction cascade are expressed in and around cephalopod chromatophores, and the longfin squid carries an unexpected diversity of photoreceptor classes.
routes.difficulty: The MACHINERY is demonstrated by expression and localisation. That the skin uses it to drive chromatophores is an inference the authors state as a suggestion ('suggest dermal photoreception'), not a measured behaviour.

evidence.cite: Kingston AC et al. 2015, J Exp Biol 218:1596-602, 'Visual phototransduction components in cephalopod chromatophores suggest dermal photoreception'
Kingston AC et al. 2015, PLoS One 10:e0135381, 'An Unexpected Diversity of Photoreceptor Classes in the Longfin Squid, Doryteuthis pealeii'

routes.title: Change the inhibitory surround that spaces new chromatophores
routes.intervention: Alter the size, or the age-dependence of the size, of the hypothetical inhibitory field each chromatophore projects around itself.
routes.predicted_phenotype: A different array layout at the same density: varying the surround in the published simulation generates other known cephalopod distributions, including the clustered units seen in some squid species.
routes.mechanism: New chromatophores are inserted far from existing ones; a sigmoidal inhibitory surround whose size changes with age reproduces the measured spacing of new versus old units.
routes.difficulty: High. The surround is HYPOTHETICAL: it is a term in a simulation fitted to spacing measurements, with no molecule attached to it.

evidence.cite: Reiter S et al. 2018, Nature 562:361-366, 'Elucidating the control and development of skin patterning in cuttlefish'

routes.title: Change the insertion rate and watch the colour ratio defend itself
routes.intervention: Alter skin growth rate or the fraction of existing chromatophores that seeds new ones per day.
routes.predicted_phenotype: The light-to-dark ratio should move - and in the wild type it does not: it stays at 1.06 +/- 0.19 to 1 across animals from 8 to 252 days old, while insertion falls from 4.1%/day at 7 days to 0.6%/day at 105 days and the light-state lifetime rises from about 19 to about 97 days.
routes.mechanism: Insertion rate and light-state lifetime are balanced along a curve the authors derive analytically, and the measured pairs fall on it.
routes.lethality_risk: None - longitudinal imaging of behaving animals.
routes.difficulty: The MEASUREMENT is done and is excellent. The INTERVENTION is proposed: nobody has perturbed either quantity.

evidence.cite: Reiter S et al. 2018, Nature 562:361-366, 'Elucidating the control and development of skin patterning in cuttlefish'
Yacob J et al. 2011, J Exp Biol 214:3423-32, 'Principles underlying chromatophore addition during maturation in the European cuttlefish, Sepia officinalis'

routes.title: Re-innervate chromatophores as they change colour class
routes.intervention: Test whether a chromatophore's motor neuron is swapped when the cell transitions from the light to the dark class at about 19 days.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Motor units stay monochromatic across the animal's life without the animal having to track each unit's age.
routes.mechanism: If new motor neurons innervated only newly born light chromatophores, the animal would need to know each unit's age to keep units colour-pure. Re-innervation removes that requirement.
routes.difficulty: Open. The supporting observation is indirect - red (transitioning) chromatophores have smaller mean diameter and smaller size variance than light or dark ones - and the authors present it as a hypothesis.

evidence.cite: Reiter S et al. 2018, Nature 562:361-366, 'Elucidating the control and development of skin patterning in cuttlefish'

routes.editorial_note: Written, cut to meet a route-count range, then restored when that range turned out to be a floor. See NOTES.md for the reason it was nearly cut.

routes.title: Grow the array a hundredfold while keeping it addressable
routes.intervention: The developmental problem itself: go from a few thousand chromatophores in a hatchling to a few millions before death, with new units inserted daily into a stretching sheet, without the control map going stale.
routes.predicted_phenotype: An addressable array whose addresses survive an order-of-magnitude change in element count. No engineered display has this property and none needs it.
routes.mechanism: Local insertion rules plus (hypothesised) re-innervation, with no global coordinate system anywhere in the account.
routes.difficulty: This is the part of the design space with the least engineering competition and, we think, the most transferable idea in it.

evidence.cite: Reiter S et al. 2018, Nature 562:361-366, 'Elucidating the control and development of skin patterning in cuttlefish'
Yacob J et al. 2011, J Exp Biol 214:3423-32, 'Principles underlying chromatophore addition during maturation in the European cuttlefish, Sepia officinalis'

routes.title: Use Euprymna berryi as the transgenic chassis
routes.intervention: Adopt E. berryi: large embryo numbers, culturable through the whole life cycle, sequenced genome, and an existing germline knockout line.
routes.predicted_phenotype: A cephalopod in which edits can be made, bred and recovered - the precondition for everything else on the cephalopod side.
routes.mechanism: n/a - a platform choice.
routes.difficulty: Demonstrated for knockout. Not demonstrated for anything that ADDS a function.

evidence.cite: Ahuja N et al. 2023, Curr Biol 33:2774-2783.e5, 'Creation of an albino squid line by CRISPR-Cas9 and its application for in vivo functional imaging of neural activity'
Gavriouchkina D et al. 2025, Nat Ecol Evol 9:1245-1262, 'A single-cell atlas of the bobtail squid visual and nervous system highlights molecular principles of convergent evolution'
evidence.note: a bobtail squid (Euprymna) atlas; the other published cephalopod cell-type atlas is Loligo vulgaris, a different animal, and is cited only under gen-find-the-promoter

routes.title: Use Doryteuthis pealeii for high-efficiency embryo editing
routes.intervention: CRISPR-Cas9 in D. pealeii embryos, where knockout efficiency routinely exceeds 90%.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Efficient F0 knockouts, in the species with the best-characterised chromatophore physiology and the largest axons.
routes.mechanism: n/a.
routes.difficulty: Demonstrated for F0. The species is not closed-life-cycle in culture, so there is no germline route in it - a real split from E. berryi.

evidence.cite: Crawford K et al. 2020, Curr Biol 30:3484-3490.e4, 'Highly Efficient Knockout of a Squid Pigmentation Gene'

routes.title: Express ANY transgene in a cephalopod chromatophore
routes.intervention: Deliver a chromatophore-specific promoter driving any protein - a fluorophore, a channelrhodopsin, a designer receptor - into a cephalopod and show it is expressed in the right cell.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Nothing yet. This has not been demonstrated.
routes.mechanism: n/a.
routes.difficulty: This is the gate. Every cephalopod route that ADDS a controllable element - optogenetic drive, a designer receptor, an engineered reflectin, a reporter of motor-unit identity - is downstream of this one step, and the step has no published precedent we found. Both demonstrated cephalopod manipulations delete a gene; neither expresses one.

evidence.cite: Crawford K et al. 2020, Curr Biol 30:3484-3490.e4, 'Highly Efficient Knockout of a Squid Pigmentation Gene'
Ahuja N et al. 2023, Curr Biol 33:2774-2783.e5, 'Creation of an albino squid line by CRISPR-Cas9 and its application for in vivo functional imaging of neural activity'
Duruz J et al. 2023, Elife 12, 'Molecular characterization of cell types in the squid Loligo vulgaris'

species_of_evidence: none - this has not been done in any cephalopod

routes.title: Mine single-cell atlases for a chromatophore-specific promoter
routes.intervention: Mine the published cephalopod single-cell atlases - cell types in Loligo vulgaris, and a bobtail squid visual and nervous system atlas - for genes expressed in chromatophore muscle or pigment cells and nowhere else, then test their regulatory regions.
routes.predicted_phenotype: A candidate promoter that drives expression in chromatophores specifically - the missing reagent for the route above.
routes.mechanism: Cell-type-resolved transcriptomes give candidate marker genes; their upstream regions are candidate drivers.
routes.difficulty: Feasible now and, as far as we found, not yet done. Two cautions. The inference from 'expressed specifically' to 'its promoter drives specifically' is exactly the inference that fails often enough to need testing. And neither atlas is in the species with the germline route: the cell-type atlas is Loligo vulgaris and the nervous-system atlas is a bobtail squid, while the only heritable knockout line is Euprymna berryi, so a promoter found in one animal has to be shown to work in another.

evidence.cite: Duruz J et al. 2023, Elife 12, 'Molecular characterization of cell types in the squid Loligo vulgaris'
Gavriouchkina D et al. 2025, Nat Ecol Evol 9:1245-1262, 'A single-cell atlas of the bobtail squid visual and nervous system highlights molecular principles of convergent evolution'
Albertin CB et al. 2015, Nature 524:220-4, 'The octopus genome and the evolution of cephalopod neural and morphological novelties'

routes.title: Put melanopsin in a melanophore and command it with light
routes.intervention: Express Opn4x under a melanophore promoter in zebrafish and project patterned blue light.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Cell-autonomous pigment dispersion (darkening) of individual melanophores under blue light, reversible in the dark, with the spatial pattern set by the projector.
routes.mechanism: Melanopsin drives dispersion in Xenopus melanophores through phospholipase C and calcium; zebrafish melanophores carry the same dynein/kinesin melanosome transport machinery.
routes.difficulty: Each half is demonstrated in a different animal; the combination is not. Note the authors' own complication: in Xenopus the IN VITRO response is direct and dispersing, while the IN VIVO embryo response needs the eye and pituitary alpha-MSH and goes the other way. We keep both readings.

evidence.cite: Moraes MN et al. 2015, Photochem Photobiol 91:1133-41, 'Melanopsins: Localization and Phototransduction in Xenopus laevis Melanophores'

Bertolesi GE et al. 2015, Pigment Cell Melanoma Res 28:559-71, 'Melanopsin photoreception in the eye regulates light-induced skin colour changes through the production of α-MSH in the pituitary gland'
evidence.note: the in vivo route disagrees with the in vitro one; both kept

evidence.cite: Semenova I et al. 2014, Mol Biol Cell 25:3119-32, 'Regulation of microtubule-based transport by MAP4'
Hasegawa S et al. 2019, Sci Rep 9:5099, 'Investigation of multiple-dynein transport of melanosomes by non-invasive force measurement using fluctuation unit χ'

routes.title: Drive melanophores with a designer receptor and a designer ligand
routes.intervention: Express a Gi-coupled DREADD in melanophores and dose the animal with its ligand.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Ligand-dependent, dose-graded melanosome aggregation - a pale animal on command.
routes.mechanism: Alpha-2 adrenoceptors, which are Gi-coupled, predominantly mediate aggregation in tilapia melanophores; a designer Gi receptor should enter the same pathway.
routes.difficulty: The inference from 'alpha-2 aggregates' to 'any Gi receptor aggregates' is the weak link, and it is OUR inference, not the source's. The field also disagrees about cAMP's sign: PACAP raises cAMP and AGGREGATES tilapia melanophores, which the authors themselves call paradoxical, while in zebrafish cAMP/PKA disperses.

evidence.cite: Acharya LS & Ovais M 2007, Indian J Exp Biol 45:984-91, 'Alpha1 and alpha2 adrenoceptor mediated melanosome aggregatory responses in vitro in Oreochromis mossambica (Peters) melanophores'

routes.title: Scramble and re-form a pigment pattern with channelrhodopsin
routes.intervention: Blue light on transgenic zebrafish melanophores expressing a ChR2 variant.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Melanophores depolarise and MIGRATE at random, disarranging xanthophores and iridophores too; the pattern re-forms when the light goes off. Works in young and adult fish but not at about 5 weeks post-fertilisation.
routes.mechanism: Depolarisation drives cell migration. It is a cell-MOVEMENT tool, not a colour-change tool, and the paper reports no melanosome transport readout.
routes.lethality_risk: None reported; the light is not harmful to the cells.
routes.difficulty: Demonstrated. Included because it is the ONLY published optogenetic chromatophore experiment we found, and it is important that what it controls is position, not colour.

evidence.cite: Aramaki T & Kondo S 2020, Dev Biol 460:12-19, 'Method for disarranging the pigment pattern of zebrafish by optogenetics'

routes.title: Dial iridophore number up or down with one receptor gene
routes.intervention: Use shady (ltk loss of function) or the dominant moonstone allele ltk-mne, or an inducible ltk transgene.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Loss: no silvery iridophores and an abnormal stripe pattern. Gain: ectopic iridophores and silvery patches.
routes.mechanism: Ltk controls iridophore establishment, proliferation and survival cell-autonomously, with evidence for homotypic competition.
routes.reversibility: None for an allele; an inducible transgene would be.
routes.difficulty: Demonstrated both ways. The closest thing in any animal to a single-gene dial on a structural-colour cell type.

evidence.cite: Lopes SS et al. 2008, PLoS Genet 4:e1000026, 'Leukocyte tyrosine kinase functions in pigment cell development'
Fadeev A et al. 2016, Pigment Cell Melanoma Res 29:284-96, 'Zebrafish Leucocyte tyrosine kinase controls iridophore establishment, proliferation and survival'

routes.title: Reprogram the skin pattern itself with connexin41.8 variants
routes.intervention: Transgenic expression of Cx41.8 or its mutants under the mitfa promoter.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Narrow stripes with wide interstripes, narrow stripes with narrow interstripes, a labyrinth, or a leopard (donut-ring) pattern - the last predicted in advance by a Turing model.
routes.mechanism: Gap-junction coupling between pigment cells sets the wavelength of a reaction-diffusion-like pigment-cell network.
routes.difficulty: Demonstrated, and it is the only route in this whole design space where a quantitative model PREDICTED a pattern before it was made. It changes the standing layout, not the runtime state, so it is a development route in a vertebrate body.

evidence.cite: Watanabe M & Kondo S 2012, Pigment Cell Melanoma Res 25:326-30, 'Changing clothes easily: connexin41.8 regulates skin pattern variation'

routes.title: Start from a transparent fish so your actuator is the only thing visible
routes.intervention: Use tyrb;csf1ra;pnp4a ('amber') or tyrb;csf1ra;tfec ('ruby') triple mutant tilapia, or a zebrafish nacre/csf1ra background.
routes.predicted_phenotype: A medium-sized fish with no visible pigment cells, so any introduced colour element is unambiguous. Note the honest caveat in the source: amber stops being transparent at 60 dpf as iridophores recover, and ruby at 120 dpf as the body wall thickens.
routes.mechanism: Sequential removal of xanthophores, erythrophores, pigmented melanophores and reflective platelets by multi-gene CRISPR mutation and crossing.
routes.lethality_risk: Low - lines are viable and used for in vivo imaging.
routes.difficulty: Demonstrated. The time-limited transparency is a real constraint on any experiment that needs an adult.

evidence.cite: Liang G et al. 2025, N Biotechnol 89:163-176, 'Creation of colorless transparent tilapia using CRISPR/Cas9 mediated multi-gene mutation'

routes.title: Find out how fast a vertebrate chromatophore can actually be driven
routes.intervention: Measure single-cell melanosome aggregation and dispersion time constants under neural and hormonal drive, which we could not find reported.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Unknown, and that is the point. The fastest vertebrate figure we found is whole-body: Nassau groupers change pattern in 4.44 s mean (range 0.97-9.87 s), with the fastest contrast changes under 1 s, which the authors read as direct neural control. Compare a cephalopod chromatophore: peak expansion 117-150 ms after a startle flash, of which only 67-83 ms is the actuator itself and 50-67 ms is sensory and neural latency.
routes.mechanism: Microtubule motor transport of melanosomes, rather than muscle, sets the vertebrate timescale.
routes.difficulty: Cheap and apparently not done. SCOPE OF THE NEGATIVE: no melanosome-level time constant appeared in any ABSTRACT we read, across PubMed searches for tilapia melanophore aggregation, melanosome aggregation kinetics and Xenopus melanophore dispersion. No full texts were fetched, and older physiology literature was not searched. The positive control is that the same searches returned relevant papers.

evidence.cite: Watson AC et al. 2014, J Fish Biol 85:1634-49, 'Dynamic camouflage by Nassau groupers Epinephelus striatus on a Caribbean coral reef'
Hadjisolomou SP et al. 2021, Front Physiol 12:675252, 'Quantifying the Speed of Chromatophore Activity at the Single-Organ Level in Response to a Visual Startle Stimulus in Living, Intact Squid'
Chen SC et al. 2013, PLoS One 8:e70342, 'Possible involvement of cone opsins in distinct photoresponses of intrinsically photosensitive dermal chromatophores in tilapia Oreochromis niloticus'
Yoshioka S et al. 2011, J R Soc Interface 8:56-66, 'Mechanism of variable structural colour in the neon tetra: quantitative evaluation of the Venetian blind model'

routes.title: Build the sheet out of silicon and thermochromic dye instead
routes.intervention: A 1.4 cm, 16x16 pixel flexible sheet with multiplexed photodetectors and silicon diode heaters under a thermochromic dye layer.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Autonomous black-to-white pattern matching to the surroundings, switching in 1-2 s at 10.5-11.5 V, with distributed sensing and actuation in one laminate.
routes.mechanism: Diode heating crosses the dye's 47 C threshold; photodetectors in the same laminate close the loop.
routes.difficulty: Built in 2014. This is the comparator every biological route has to beat, and on 'changes appearance on command' it already wins.

evidence.cite: Yu C et al. 2014, Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A 111:12998-3003, 'Adaptive optoelectronic camouflage systems with designs inspired by cephalopod skins'

routes.title: Pump coloured fluid through channels in a silicone skin
routes.intervention: Microfluidic networks moulded into a soft elastomer body, perfused with dyed or temperature-controlled fluids.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Colour, contrast, pattern, apparent shape, luminescence and surface temperature all changed - and changed SIMULTANEOUSLY in the visible and the infrared, which the authors note no organism can do.
routes.mechanism: Bulk transport of a coloured fluid, rather than any local actuator.
routes.difficulty: Built in 2012. Tethered to pumps, and the response time was not reported in the abstract we read.

evidence.cite: Morin SA et al. 2012, Science 337:828-32, 'Camouflage and display for soft machines'

routes.editorial_note: Written, cut to meet a route-count range, then restored when that range turned out to be a floor. See NOTES.md for the reason it was nearly cut.

routes.title: Make an artificial chromatophore from a dielectric elastomer
routes.intervention: A pigmented dielectric elastomer actuator that expands a coloured area under high voltage.
routes.predicted_phenotype: 33-42% area change in the published modelling, needing about 5.6 kV, with a viscoelastic relaxation time around 3 s. Compare a real chromatophore: +155% area, reached 117-150 ms after a startle flash, of which the actuator's own expansion phase is 67-83 ms.
routes.mechanism: Maxwell stress thins and stretches the elastomer, spreading the pigment.
routes.difficulty: The honest comparison is unflattering to the mimic: it is four times smaller in stroke and twenty times slower than the biological actuator, and it wants kilovolts. These numbers come from a MODEL; we did not obtain measured values from the experimental paper's abstract.

evidence.cite: Fishman A et al. 2015, J R Soc Interface 12:20150281, 'Hiding the squid: patterns in artificial cephalopod skin'
Rossiter J et al. 2012, Bioinspir Biomim 7:036009, 'Biomimetic chromatophores for camouflage and soft active surfaces'

routes.title: Express reflectin in a human cell and make it optically dynamic
routes.intervention: Reflectin A1 in HEK293 cells, reconfigured with 100 mM NaCl and imaged by quantitative phase microscopy.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Reflectin particles grow from about 400 to about 800 nm over an hour and their refractive index moves within 1.41-1.52. It is a change in refractive index and particle size, NOT a demonstrated colour change, and the paper does not claim one.
routes.mechanism: Salt screens reflectin's charge, driving the same condensation that phosphorylation drives in a squid iridophore.
routes.reversibility: Partially; cycling was not the focus.
routes.difficulty: Demonstrated. The gap between 'the protein assembles in a human cell' and 'the cell changes colour' is the whole remaining problem.

evidence.cite: Bogdanov G et al. 2023, iScience 26:106854, 'Squid leucophore-inspired engineering of optically dynamic human cells'

routes.title: Switch a reflectin film with a voltage instead of a kinase
routes.intervention: Apply -0.55 to -0.8 V to a hydrated recombinant reflectin thin film.
routes.predicted_phenotype: The film shrinks by 8-15 nm and its refractive index rises by 0.022-0.045, over 30 cycles. That is a real but small tuning: the best protein-film spectral shift anyone has reported is about 11 nm, against the 250 nm range a live iridophore covers.
routes.mechanism: Electrochemical reduction of histidine residues substitutes for phosphorylation in neutralising charge and driving assembly.
routes.difficulty: Demonstrated in vitro. The films (45-91 nm) are far thinner than a Bragg stack, so this is a materials result, not yet a reflector.

evidence.cite: Lin YC et al. 2025, Adv Mater 37:e2411005, 'Electrochemically Driven Optical Dynamics of Reflectin Protein Films'
Liang SP et al. 2020, J R Soc Interface 17:20200774, 'Electrochemistry as a surrogate for protein phosphorylation: voltage-controlled assembly of reflectin A1'
Wolde-Michael E et al. 2021, Sci Rep 11:14580, 'Design and fabrication of recombinant reflectin-based multilayer reflectors: bio-design engineering and photoisomerism induced wavelength modulation'

routes.title: Give up on visible colour and modulate the infrared instead
routes.intervention: A mechanically actuated squid-skin-inspired composite, strained 0-50%.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Infrared transmittance switches on/off by a factor of about 25 (1% to 25%), regulating about 36 W/m2 of heat flux for about 3 W/m2 of mechanical input, stable over 1000 cycles.
routes.mechanism: Strain opens gaps in a reflective metal layer on an elastomer.
routes.difficulty: Built, and already in a wearable demonstrator. It is the most commercially advanced thing in this list, and it works precisely because it abandoned the hard problem (visible colour) for an easier one.

evidence.cite: Xu C et al. 2018, Science 359:1495-1500, 'Adaptive infrared-reflecting systems inspired by cephalopods'
Leung EM et al. 2019, Nat Commun 10:1947, 'A dynamic thermoregulatory material inspired by squid skin'
Phan L et al. 2013, Adv Mater 25:5621-5, 'Reconfigurable infrared camouflage coatings from a cephalopod protein'

routes.title: Change the texture rather than the colour
routes.intervention: Elastomeric membranes with embedded inextensible textile mesh, inflated pneumatically, after the papilla musculature of cuttlefish.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Flat sheets transform into programmed 3D shapes within 10% of their targets, imitating stones and plants.
routes.mechanism: A fibre-reinforced membrane's inflated shape is set by the mesh pattern, so the target shape can be designed backwards.
routes.difficulty: Demonstrated. Included because cuttlefish papillae are a SEPARATE actuator system from chromatophores, neurally controlled and capable of holding a shape for an hour without continuous input, and the engineering mimic got there first.

evidence.cite: Pikul JH et al. 2017, Science 358:210-214, 'Stretchable surfaces with programmable 3D texture morphing for synthetic camouflaging skins'
Gonzalez-Bellido PT et al. 2018, iScience 1:24-34, 'Neural Control of Dynamic 3-Dimensional Skin Papillae for Cuttlefish Camouflage'

routes.title: Pattern a fluorescent skin with light rather than electricity
routes.intervention: Photomechanically modulated display layers that pattern fluorescence on demand.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Arbitrary fluorescent patterns written optically into a soft sheet, with no per-pixel wiring at all.
routes.mechanism: A photomechanical layer changes the geometry that gates the fluorophore's emission.
routes.reversibility: Reported as on-demand patterning; cycling limits not read.
routes.difficulty: Demonstrated. Relevant to the control-channel question from the other side: optical addressing removes the wiring problem entirely, which is the problem every biological route spends its effort on.

evidence.cite: Shi H et al. 2021, Advanced materials (Deerfield Beach, Fla.) , 'Cephalopod-Inspired Design of Photomechanically Modulated Display Systems for On-Demand Fluorescent Patterning.'
Wang Q et al. 2014, Nature communications , 'Cephalopod-inspired design of electro-mechano-chemically responsive elastomers for on-demand fluorescent patterning.'
Han D et al. 2021, ACS applied materials & interfaces , 'Multimaterial Printing for Cephalopod-Inspired Light-Responsive Artificial Chromatophores.'

routes.editorial_note: Written, cut to meet a route-count range, then restored when that range turned out to be a floor. See NOTES.md for the reason it was nearly cut.

routes.title: Benchmark against a commercial electrophoretic panel
routes.intervention: None - this is the yardstick.
routes.predicted_phenotype: A commercial reflective panel at 300 pixels per inch, i.e. about 85 um pitch, which is comparable to a cuttlefish chromatophore's 15-100 um diameter. Update time, contrast and power are not on the public product page, so we do not state them.
routes.mechanism: Electrophoretic migration of charged pigment particles in a microcapsule.
routes.difficulty: On sale. The design-space consequence is blunt: on spatial resolution the engineered article already matches the animal, so a biological programmable skin has to justify itself on something else - self-repair, self-assembly, growth, or power.

evidence.cite: E Ink ED060KHE 6-inch Carta 1300 product page
evidence.note: Only the resolution and pixel density were on the page; the pitch is our arithmetic from 300 ppi, and is labelled as such.

recommendation.Why this one: Not because it is the most interesting result, but because it is the only route that unblocks the others. Exactly two genetic manipulations have been demonstrated in any cephalopod chromatophore system, and both DELETE a pigment gene: tdo knockout in Doryteuthis pealeii (2020) and tdo+ido double knockout giving a heritable albino Euprymna berryi line (2023). You cannot build an addressable skin by deleting things. Every cephalopod route in this space that ADDS a controllable element - an optogenetic drive on a radial muscle, a designer receptor, an engineered reflectin, a reporter that labels one motor unit - requires expressing a transgene in a chromatophore, and we found no published instance of a transgene being expressed in a cephalopod at all. Counted rather than guessed, and the count is computed in `validation.cephalopod_routes_nobody_can_take` rather than asserted here: of the 30 cephalopod-scale routes on this page, twelve are ones nobody can currently take. One of those twelve is this step itself and one is our own controller-sizing study, which needs no animal. The other TEN are downstream of expressing a transgene - as is every future route of that kind. The reagents now exist to try: a germline-competent species with a closed life cycle, published single-cell atlases to mine for a chromatophore-specific promoter, and a working delivery route. Until this lands, the cephalopod half of this page is a reading list.
recommendation.What we would fund second: circ-size-the-controller and the measurement that feeds it. The control layer is the part of this system that is genuinely novel as engineering - a chromatophore is about four independent actuators, not one, and real pattern transitions live on a 9-dimensional manifold out of 17,305 - and it is measurable today with video and no genetics at all.
recommendation.The route we would NOT fund: Anything whose goal is a wider tunable range in the reflector. Our own optical model says the measured 425-675 nm range already spans the useful band and widening it buys 1% of gamut, while refractive-index contrast buys 68%.
recommendation.If the goal is a product rather than a r: Buy the non-living route. A 16x16 autonomously colour-matching optoelectronic sheet was built in 2014 and switches in 1-2 s; commercial electrophoretic panels run at 300 ppi, a pitch comparable to a real chromatophore's. On 'skin that changes appearance on command', the engineered article already wins. The biology's contribution right now is the design brief - what to aim for, and which axes are hard - not the substrate.
recommendation.What would change our mind: A single published transgene expressed in a cephalopod chromatophore. That one result moves the ten routes counted above from unreachable to attemptable, opens the class of routes that cannot be written down yet because nobody can try them, and nothing else on the horizon does.

welfare.status: Cephalopods are the invertebrates most often brought inside research-animal regulation, and the literature treats them that way: papers on this list include dedicated anaesthesia studies framed explicitly as welfare contributions. We did not read any legal instrument and make no claim about what any particular jurisdiction requires.
welfare.anaesthesia: Magnesium chloride and ethanol have been assessed in Euprymna berryi embryos; isoflurane has been assessed dose-dependently in Octopus vulgaris and described by its authors as a contribution to cephalopod welfare. Both are pilot or dose-finding studies, not settled protocols.
welfare.what the routes here actually cost: Most circuit-scale routes on this page are terminal or near-terminal: motor-unit mapping is done on freshly dissected skin, single-motoneuron stimulation needs an opened animal, and optic-lobe microstimulation is invasive brain work. The developmental and behavioural routes are not - Reiter et al. tracked 17,305 chromatophores in freely behaving animals with nothing more invasive than a camera, which is worth noting because it produced the single most useful control-layer number on this page.
welfare.the sedation question: Renard et al. checked whether sedation changed their result and it did not (3.715 +/- 1.211 independent components per chromatophore sedated versus 3.683 +/- 1.224 head-fixed and unsedated, p = 0.83). That control is worth copying: it is the difference between a welfare measure and a confound.
welfare.vertebrate alternative: If the goal is a demonstration rather than cephalopod biology specifically, zebrafish and tilapia routes reach a comparable result in an animal with established husbandry, established welfare frameworks and reversible, non-invasive actuation (light on, light off).
welfare.non-living alternative: Several routes here involve no animal at all and reach the headline capability faster. That is an uncomfortable thing for a biology page to say and we think it should be said first, not last.

limitations: A count of routes with direct cephalopod evidence flatters this page, and the `validation` block is built to stop it doing that. Every route carries a `route_kind` as well as an evidence strength, and the cross-tab is computed. The number that matters is `addressable_runtime_control`: how many routes give a dial you could actually use in a working skin - addressed to a place, changeable second by second. Read that field before anything else on this page. In a cephalopod the only entries are electrode stimulations of a dissected or opened preparation, which is not a programmable skin; it is a way of finding out how one would work.

Cephalopod causal genetics rests on two papers. Crawford et al. 2020 and Ahuja et al. 2023 are the entire demonstrated repertoire, both knockouts of the same pigment pathway. Treating this as a 'literature' would be wrong.

We read the full text of six sources and the abstract of most of the rest. An abstract-level read is recorded as such on every evidence item. Several numbers quoted here - the tilapia transparency timings, the Gorodetsky IR figures, the DEA area changes - come from abstracts, and an abstract's numbers are the ones the authors chose to headline.

The two engineering sources with no PubMed record in the earlier survey (the Rogers optoelectronic sheet, the Whitesides microfluidic skin) do in fact have PMIDs, 25136094 and 22904008, which we found and verified. Much of the remaining cephalopod optics and soft-robotics literature genuinely sits in physics and materials journals; where a source has no PMID the field is simply absent and a DOI or URL carries the citation instead. See NOTES.md.

Three routes on this page are ours rather than anyone's: the sacculus-softening route, the add-radial-muscles route and the controller-sizing route come out of our own models, and the first two depend on a sacculus stiffness that has never been measured and which our model FITS. They are labelled model_only for that reason and should not be read as predictions with evidence behind them.

We did not survey the octopus papilla literature, the deep-sea bioluminescent signalling literature, or the behavioural camouflage literature in any depth, although sources from each are in the library. The page is about the actuator, the optics and the control layer.

No route here has been costed, and several 'difficulty' fields are judgements rather than measurements. Where a difficulty claim rests on an absence ('nobody has done this'), the scope of the search that found nothing is stated in NOTES.md rather than in the route.

cephalopod_routes_nobody_can_take.note: Of these, gen-transgene-in-a-chromatophore IS the blocking step and circ-size-the-controller is our own modelling study, which needs no animal. The rest are downstream of expressing a transgene.

addressable_runtime_control.read_this_first: Ten routes on this page offer spatially addressable runtime control. Five are non-living devices. Two are vertebrate, and one of those (vert-melanopsin-light-actuator) is a combination of two results from two different animals that nobody has yet put together, while the other (vert-optogenetic-scramble) controls where a pigment cell GOES, not what colour it is. The three cephalopod entries are all electrode stimulation of dissected or opened preparations. So: in a cephalopod, the state of the art in addressing a chromatophore is a wire on a nerve in a dish. That is the honest answer to 'could you build skin that changes appearance on command', and it is why the recommended route is a reagent and not an experiment.
